subject.title: [Feature]: Pre-reset agentic memory flush — /new and daily reset should get the same memory flush as compaction

question: Should OpenClaw run a silent tool-capable memory-flush agent turn before explicit and implicit session resets, and what owner boundary/default should control it?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the fix changes reset latency and allows hidden agent/tool execution at a session lifecycle boundary, so automation cannot choose the security and product default.

options.title: Design a bounded pre-reset memory contract
options.body: Add a core-owned or memory-plugin-owned pre-reset capability that timeboxes the silent flush, preserves sandbox/approval/read-only guards, and covers explicit, daily, and idle resets.

options.title: Keep mechanical preservation only
options.body: Rely on session_end/session-memory/transcript indexing for raw backup and leave curated agentic memory to active-session compaction and ordinary turns.

options.title: Defer to broader reset UX work
options.body: Handle the user harm through warning, opt-out, or session-continuity work before adding a hidden reset-time agent turn.

recommendation.title: Design a bounded pre-reset memory contract
recommendation.body: Add a core-owned or memory-plugin-owned pre-reset capability that timeboxes the silent flush, preserves sandbox/approval/read-only guards, and covers explicit, daily, and idle resets.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest sampled history on memory flush ownership and session lifecycle hardening, making him the best available owner for the product/security direction.
